messages:
sam: Thanks everyone for the great all-hands earlier. Quick follow-up on the pricing / credits questions — I'm collecting the answers here and we'll push a short FAQ + docs updates tomorrow. If you raised a specific customer edge case, please DM me and we'll triage.

maria: For Hosted API, are rate limits enforced per-account or per-key? thinking about org-owned keys and sub-teams. :thinking:

sam: Good q — hosted rate limits are enforced per-project (not per individual key). Keys under the same project share the same quota and rate buckets.

jordan: For Dedicated customers, how do quotas interact with reserved capacity? is there a soft cap if they burst beyond reservation?

elaine: Dedicated customers commit reserved units monthly. Quotas are tenant-level; we allow configured burst (subject to policy) but any excess usage beyond reserved commits is billed as overage according to the contract. No free rollover of reserved units.

alex: Customers keep asking how to poll remaining credits programmatically — is there an endpoint we can point them to from support?

billing-bot: Tip: use the usage endpoint. Example:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage?period=month
```
Returns JSON summary with fields like tokens_used and credits_remaining. We also expose per-route breakdown.

ken: Also note the rate limit headers on API responses: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`. These headers are present for Hosted and Dedicated (unless the customer applies custom gateway overrides).

maria: What's the policy for trial credits? do we auto-upgrade or convert when they hit limits? any payment/401/402 behavior?

elaine: Trials get a fixed credit pool tied to the account. When credits are exhausted the API returns 402 with a clear error body; we email the admin and provide a CTA to upgrade. We do not auto-charge or auto-convert trials to paid plans.

jordan: Clarify: are quotas measured in tokens or by request count for reranking / embedding endpoints?

sam: Primary billing unit is tokens for text generation and embeddings; some non-token operations (e.g., fine-tune bundles or long-running batch jobs) use a job-based unit in the billing response. We'll add a table to the docs showing per-endpoint billing units.

alex: I'll update the support playbook with the 402 messaging and a checklist for reaching out to customers who hit trial limits.

maria: For docs — can we include a small snippet showing how to check usage and read headers? will make it easier for integrators.

ken: Example header snippet we can share: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 118742
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1710000000` — shows tokens left and reset timestamp.

sam: Next steps: we'll publish an FAQ + code examples, update the pricing page with clearer callouts around trial behavior and dedicated overage, and add support alerts for trial exhaustion. @maria please own the docs PR; @alex please own the support playbook changes. :thumbsup:

maria: On it — drafting PR now, aiming to post by EOD.

alex: Will add playbook changes and a short canned response for 402s.

sam: Thanks everyone — closing this thread for now. If there are follow-ups, drop them here or DM me. :wave:
